questions.q: In this capstone, how should you treat the example figures such as $3.9M closed won and 1,840 cases opened?
options: As real Harborline data you must reproduce exactly in any org
As illustrative examples; your own org's numbers will differ and the method is what matters
As Salesforce-mandated benchmarks
As values the dashboard must never exceed
questions.explain: Harborline is fictional and the numbers are illustrative so the four lessons stay consistent. Your org will show different values.

questions.q: What is the guiding rule for how many questions each report should answer?
options: Exactly one
As many as fit on one screen
At least three
It doesn't matter as long as it has a chart
questions.explain: One question per report keeps each dashboard component clear and easy to verify against its source report.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of the capstone's five-step plan?
options: Assemble the dashboard, write the question, build the report, choose the report type, choose the chart
Choose the chart, choose the report type, write the question, build the report, assemble the dashboard
Write the question, choose the report type, build the report, choose the chart, assemble the dashboard
Build the report, assemble the dashboard, choose the chart, write the question, choose the report type
questions.explain: Start from the question, pick the report type that has the fields, build the report, choose the chart, then assemble and check the dashboard.

questions.q: With a $6.0M quota, $3.9M closed won, and $4.2M of open pipeline closing this quarter, what is the pipeline coverage of the remaining gap?
options: About 0.5x
About 1.0x
About 1.5x
About 2.0x
questions.explain: The remaining gap is $6.0M minus $3.9M, or $2.1M. Dividing $4.2M of open pipeline by $2.1M gives 2.0x coverage.

questions.q: The example service baseline shows 1,840 cases opened and 1,725 closed this month. What does that imply about the backlog?
options: It grew by 115 cases
It shrank by 115 cases
It stayed the same
It cannot be determined from these two numbers
questions.explain: More cases opened than closed (1,840 minus 1,725 = 115), so the open backlog grew by 115 during the month.
